Oct 21 : Costa Rica have appointed former captain Bryan Ruiz as head coach to lead the national team's campaign to qualify for the 2030 World Cup, the Costa Rican Football Federation (FCRF) said on Wednesday. • Ruiz, 41, takes the job after two wins as interim coach, with Costa Rica beating Nicaragua 3-0 and Haiti 2-0 in the CONCACAF Nations League earlier this month • He succeeds Argentine Fernando Batista, who was dismissed in September, while Costa Rica missed out on the 2026 World Cup under former coach Miguel Herrera • Former attacking midfielder Ruiz captained Costa Rica at three consecutive World Cups before retiring in 2022

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 21 : Major stock indexes climbed on Wednesday, lifted by more strong results from AI-focused companies, while France's 10-year bond yield hit 5 per cent for the first time since 2002 due to growing concern about the country's economic outlook. The Nasdaq gained more than 1 per cent, with Super Micro shares rising 9.5 per cent after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates.  Shares of SpaceX shot up 7.8 per cent after Elon Musk said late on Tuesday that a merger of his two companies SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea." SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. AI-related shares sold off ahead of third-quarter results on investor worries about how long the AI trade can last.

"A lot of the concerns that we had over the last few weeks that sent the market lower are being alleviated," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York. Earnings "are coming in mixed to stronger than expected," which he called a relief. "Tech stocks fell hard last week on fears that the AI party is over," he said. In addition, US bond yields have been falling after their recent run higher, and US interest rate hike expectations have waned, he said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 360.21 points, or 0.69 per cent, to close at 52,856.09, the S&P 500 rose 44.60 points, or 0.58 per cent, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 278.04 points, or 1.05 per cent, to 26,702.86. After the closing bell, Meta Platforms shares gained after the Facebook owner raised the lower end of its annual spending forecast. Meta ended the regular session up 0.5 per cent. Tesla shares also rose in after-hours trading as it reported a surprise positive cash flow for the third quarter. The stock ended the regular session up 3.4 per cent.  MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe rose 7.48 points, or 0.7 per cent, to 1,137.88. The pan-European STOXX 600 index climbed 0.92 per cent. US Treasury yields edged lower, with the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note shedding 0.6 basis point to 5.111 per cent.  Stocks have slipped of late and bonds have rallied due to concerns about the effect of higher borrowing costs on AI infrastructure stocks. FRENCH BOND YIELDS RISE French bond yields rose again, with 10-year bond yields hitting a new 24-year high above 5 per cent. The premium on French yields over benchmark 10-year German Bunds has also edged back toward early October's 15-year high of nearly 160 bps. French President Emmanuel Macron vowed to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violence at protests planned in the coming days, and dismissed as "stupid" and "unacceptable" comments from some foreign leaders about the unrest.   French supermarket operator Carrefour fell about 13 per cent after it cut its guidance due to the recent protests. The euro was nearly flat at $1.1237. The US dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.14 per cent to 101.65.  The Australian dollar gained after Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser told a Citi conference that the inflation outlook looked "materially worse." The Aussie gained 0.41 per cent versus the greenback to $0.7031. Benchmark oil futures ended little changed, with investors weighing possible progress toward Russia-Ukraine talks against data showing a fall in US oil stocks. Brent crude rose 3 cents to settle at $108.82 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 67 cents, or 0.7 per cent, to settle at $97.15.

Source: Reuters

Oct 21 : Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said his side failed to apply enough pressure and adopted a "mood of defeat" after conceding early in Wednesday's 4–1 Champions League loss at Como, a result that increased scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick. Como opened the scoring in the second minute and United collapsed, with only a stoppage‑time consolation goal from Joshua Zirkzee making the scoreline slightly less severe. "We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early," Fernandes told TNT Sports. "There was not enough pressure on the ball and not many good movements off the ball. There were many things not going our way. "It's a decision from the (coaching) staff not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence," he said.

Asked if his comments amounted to criticism of Carrick's tactics, Fernandes said: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. "Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable." Carrick's position has come under increasing pressure with United now winless in seven matches. "It was more than disappointing," the 45-year-old manager told TNT Sports. "I think everybody's got to take responsibility for that. I'll take responsibility for the overall team and performance, it stops with me and I'm fine with that. "But as a supporter of this football club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say." Carrick said his side had failed to show the required intensity. "It's the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn't bring that today," he said. "I've got to apologise for the performance." Fernandes also questioned United's mentality after the early setback. "Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat," he said. United have three points from their opening three Champions League matches and host AS Roma in their next fixture in the competition.

Oct 21 : A Chinese-linked hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool to compromise IT services firm ConnectWise as part of a campaign that targeted hundreds of organizations globally, Microsoft said on Wednesday. ConnectWise did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Microsoft's conclusions, although a statement posted to the company's website on October 16 said it was "investigating recent attempts of unauthorized access associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup environment." The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Beijing regularly denies conducting or condoning cyber-enabled data theft. The hackers, which Microsoft tracks as Storm-0940, used an open-source penetration testing framework called ARTEX to carry out the campaign, Microsoft said.

There are multiple tools used to conduct penetration testing, a form of legitimate testing of the security of networks or services. ARTEX allows users to use any AI model to automate a variety of penetration testing tasks and can be configured to run autonomous tasks including reconnaissance and data exfiltration, Microsoft said.  The attack targeted organizations across a wide variety of sectors, including aerospace, defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, financial services, government, legal, manufacturing, media, military, semiconductor, software, technology, think tanks and nonprofits, Microsoft said. While the majority of the targeting was not successful, Microsoft said, Storm-0940 achieved privileged cloud persistence — or high-level access that could continue even after cleanup efforts — at many organizations in a brief time.

FAST

Oct 21 : Crocodilians — today's crocodiles, alligators, caimans and gharials and their many extinct relatives — have been a roaring success since debuting more than 240 million years ago. And new research identifies one important factor in their success — stubbornly keeping to warm climates throughout their history. In fact, the researchers said, this trait may help explain why crocs as a group survived the asteroid strike 66 million years ago that doomed the dinosaurs, along with certain physiological characteristics that make them one tough bunch of reptiles. The crocodilian evolutionary lineage, called Pseudosuchia, arose during the Triassic Period in the aftermath of Earth's worst mass extinction event at the end of the Permian, appearing on the scene millions of years before the first dinosaurs and mammals. The researchers tracked the geographic range for crocs during their entire history, guided by an evolutionary tree of more than 400 extinct and living species. They used data from more than 7,000 fossils and geographic records of modern crocs such as the alligators of Florida, saltwater crocodiles of Australia, gharials of India, caimans of Brazil and more.

They combined this information with 52 global palaeoclimate reconstructions to determine the climatic conditions under which crocs lived over time. While other groups such as dinosaurs and mammals conquered a variety of climates, the study showed that crocs consistently kept to warm climes. "Rather than continually adapting to new climatic conditions, they largely tracked suitable environments as these shifted geographically, expanding towards the poles during warmer periods and retreating towards the equator during cooler ones," said University College London vertebrate paleontologist Alfio Alessandro Chiarenza, lead author of the research published in the journal Science Advances. For example, during an exceptionally warm moment in Earth's history around 50 million years ago, Chiarenza said, crocs inhabited high-latitude regions of North America, Europe and even Antarctica. "One of the most striking patterns is the repeated expansion and contraction of suitable habitat in response to global temperature changes," Chiarenza said. While living crocs are primarily semiaquatic ambush predators, their extinct relatives included a broad diversity of forms, University College London paleontologist and study co-author Philip Mannion said. "They have occupied almost every conceivable ecological role," Chiarenza said. There were fully land-dwelling apex predators like 30-foot-long (9-meter-long) Fasolasuchus, pug-snouted herbivores like Simosuchus, armored plant-eaters like Aetosaurus, mollusk-eaters like Kuttanacaiman, filter-feeders like Mourasuchus and ocean-going types like Metriorhynchus. During the age of dinosaurs, there also were semiaquatic crocs like Deinosuchus up to 40 feet (12 meters) long that may have rivaled Tyrannosaurus in mass. "Modern crocodilians are only the surviving remnants of a once extraordinarily diverse evolutionary group," Chiarenza said. DISASTER FROM ABOVE The asteroid strike at a site called Chicxulub off the coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula at the end of the Cretaceous unleashed a global environmental cataclysm. Three-quarters of Earth's species including the dinosaurs, aside from their bird descendants, vanished. The crocs survived. "The Chicxulub impact caused a dramatic reduction in incoming sunlight, producing an impact winter and widespread environmental disruption. However, our climate simulations suggest that this cooling did not affect the availability of suitable climatic conditions equally for all groups," Chiarenza said. "Under all but the most extreme impact scenario we tested, tropical and subtropical regions retained climatic conditions suitable" for the crocs, Chiarenza said. This suggests that the longstanding association of crocs with warm and low-latitude environments may have placed some surviving populations in geographic refuges near the equator and in the subtropics where climatic conditions remained within their tolerances, Chiarenza said. For dinosaurs, there was a collapse of suitable habitat under these impact conditions. Crocs also possess physiological traits beneficial for times of environmental stress. They can enter states of dormancy to cope with harsh conditions — aestivation to survive extreme heat or drought, and brumation to withstand extreme cold. Crocs today, for instance, may dig burrows or encase themselves in hardened mud during severe droughts, slowing their heartbeat and breathing. "Following the Chicxulub impact, when sunlight was dramatically reduced and terrestrial primary productivity collapsed, the ability to reduce energy expenditure and survive periods of limited food availability could have been extremely advantageous," Chiarenza said. Crocs also are cold-blooded, while recent research points to at least some dinosaurs including Tyrannosaurus as warm-blooded. Baseline metabolic requirements for cold-blooded animals are much lower than for comparably sized warm-blooded animals. "That can become a significant advantage when food becomes scarce. Crocodilians can survive extended periods without feeding," Chiarenza said. "But even if an animal can survive prolonged starvation, it still needs environmental conditions that remain within its physiological limits."

Source: Reuters
